transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, well, I guess what really brought me in is that my mind just... it won't stay on one thing anymore. Like, I'll be at my bench—I do custom jewelry and metalwork—and I'll jump from reading a customer email to noticing a tiny saw mark on a ring. Which, honestly, the saw blades I've been getting lately are just terrible quality. I buy them in bulk from this supplier in Ohio, and I swear they changed the manufacturing process because they snap if you even look at them wrong. My buddy who does leatherwork says the exact same thing is happening with his tools. It's like nobody cares about quality control anymore, you know? 

But anyway... I'll be looking at the saw mark, and then I hear a noise outside, like a truck or something, and suddenly I realize I’ve completely lost the whole work order I was supposed to be focusing on. I just... I can't keep a thought straight.
Do you often find it hard to focus on tasks or activities, even outside of work—like at home or while running errands?

At home? Or errands... I mean, I don't really know if I notice it the same way. Like, I went to the hardware store the other day to get some new pliers, because my old ones got this weird rust on the joint. Which is crazy because I keep my workspace bone dry, you know? I even run a dehumidifier. It's this heavy-duty one I got off Craigslist from a guy who used to dry out basements for a living. He had this insane story about a flooded house out in Dayton... completely ruined the foundation, the whole house had to be condemned. 

But anyway, I was at the hardware store, and they had moved the whole hand tool section. Why do stores do that? You get used to a layout, and then bam, it's like a maze. I ended up standing there looking at the garden hoses for like twenty minutes because they had these new expandable ones. Have you seen those? They shrink up when the water is off. But I don't even have a yard, I rent an apartment on the second floor, so I don't know why I was even looking at them... what were you asking about? Errands?
Do you ever find yourself getting overly focused on something that isn't related to what you're supposed to be doing, like spending a lot of time looking at garden hoses when you went to buy pliers?

Yeah, I mean... exactly. That's actually what I was trying to say earlier about why I came in today. It's like my brain is just a pinball machine right now. I'll be sitting at my bench, right? And I'll be trying to read an email from a customer—this lady wants a custom silver pendant for her daughter's graduation, which is fine, but she keeps changing the design every two days. First she wanted a moon, then a star, now she wants a whole constellation. I mean, silver is expensive right now, the market is crazy. My buddy was telling me that investors are hoarding it because they think the dollar is going to tank. He watches all these financial channels on YouTube. Some of those guys are just yelling into a microphone, but you know, sometimes they make a good point about inflation. 

But yeah, I'll be looking at that email, and then I'll notice a tiny saw mark on a piece of metal, and then I'll hear a truck outside—they're doing roadwork on my street, tearing up the asphalt, it smells like tar all day—and suddenly I realize I've completely lost the work order I was supposed to be focusing on. My mind just will not stay on one single thing.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself needing to be constantly moving, like you can't sit still for very long?

Yeah, exactly, it's like I can't even stay in my chair. I couldn't sit still at the bench at all lately. I'd bounce from sketching this new watch case idea I had—which, by the way, vintage watch cases are making a huge comeback. I saw this guy on Instagram restoring these old 1940s Hamiltons, and the craftsmanship is just unbelievable. They used to actually care about the mechanics back then, you know? Now everything is just cheap quartz movements stamped out in a factory. It's sad, really. My grandfather had a pocket watch that he passed down to my dad, but my dad lost it when we moved to Chicago. We had this terrible moving company, completely disorganized, they broke half our plates too. 

But yeah, I'd be sketching the watch case, and then I'd jump up to email suppliers, and then next thing I know I'm rearranging all my display trays... and this is like, long after I was supposed to be done for the day, way past closing. I just... I have to keep moving.
Do you find yourself acting quickly without thinking things through, like making sudden decisions or saying things impulsively that you later regret?

Impulsive? Uh, I don't know if I'd say I do things without thinking, really. I mean, I guess I make decisions fast, but that's just because I know what I want. Like the other day, I was at this estate sale. Estate sales are the best place to find raw materials, honestly. People just throw away old sterling silverware sets for nothing because nobody wants to polish them anymore. It's crazy. This one house, the guy must have been a collector or something, because he had all these antique brass lamps. Beautiful patina on them. I was talking to the lady running the sale—she had this little poodle that kept yapping at everyone's ankles, one of those really nervous dogs, you know? I had a dog like that growing up, a terrier mix, he would bark at the mailman like it was his full-time job. 

Anyway, I bought this whole box of random metal scrap from her, just handed her the cash. I didn't even really look through the whole box first. I mean, maybe that's impulsive? But I don't really regret it, you know? I usually find something good in those boxes. What were we talking about? Regretting things?
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high, irritable, or energized lately—like feeling on top of the world or more confident than usual?

Yeah, I guess you could say that. Like, we had this local craft and jewelry show last weekend, right? And normally I just set up my booth and hope for the best, but this time... man, after the show, I just felt completely lit up. Like I was larger than life, you know? I felt like I could take on the whole industry. The industry is so cutthroat right now, especially with all these online retailers drop-shipping cheap alloy rings from overseas and calling them "artisanal." It really undercuts guys like me who actually work with our hands. My hands are always covered in polishing compound, by the way. Rouge gets everywhere. It's this red paste, and if you don't wear an apron, it ruins your clothes. I had to throw out three good shirts last month because my washing machine just couldn't get the stains out. The washing machine is making this weird clanking noise during the spin cycle anyway, I probably need to call a repair guy. But those guys charge like a hundred bucks just to show up. 

But yeah, I was feeling so energized, just on top of the world. But then, if anyone tried to tell me to, I don't know, stick to normal shop hours or slow down, I just snapped at them. Like, my sister came by and told me I needed to sleep, and I just bit her head off. I didn't have time to slow down, I was onto something big. But yeah, definitely feeling... elevated, I guess.
Can you describe how long you felt that way during the craft show? Did it feel like a distinct period where your mood was really different from your usual self?

Yeah, it was definitely a distinct period. It started right after I got this award at the jewelry show—Best in Show for Metalwork, which was honestly a huge surprise because the judges usually go for that really delicate filigree stuff. Filigree is so tedious, you have to twist these tiny little wires together, and honestly, it just looks too fragile to me. I prefer chunky, solid pieces, like brutalist style. Anyway, right after they handed me the ribbon, this... this wired, completely out-of-control stretch started. And it just kept going. It lasted for about two weeks, just this intense, non-stop energy. Two whole weeks of just... going. I didn't even put the ribbon up in my shop, actually. It's still sitting in the glovebox of my truck. My truck needs an oil change so bad, the light's been on for like three days. I keep meaning to take it to that place down on 4th Street, but they always try to upsell you on air filters and wiper blades. Like, buddy, I can change my own wiper blades, it takes two seconds. But yeah, two weeks of feeling totally wired and different from my usual self.
